name: simple-workflow
title: Simple Workflow
description: Pick one ClinicalTrials.gov NCT id from a fixed list of five studies, download every document the study has posted (protocol, SAP, ICF), have an agent extract CDISC USDM study-definition metadata from those documents, render its schedule of activities as an interactive table that shows gaps as gaps, and put both in front of a human reviewer.

steps.name: Select Study
steps.description: Choose the NCT id of the study this run works on.

params.name: nctId
params.description: ClinicalTrials.gov registry identifier of the selected study

steps.name: Fetch Study Documents
steps.description: Ask the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API which documents the selected study has posted and download each one into the step output.

steps.name: Generate USDM Metadata
steps.description: AI. Reads the protocol (and SAP / ICF when present) downloaded by Fetch Study Documents out of the run workspace, extracts the study definition, and writes CDISC USDM v3.0.0 metadata as usdm.json, with usdm-provenance.json for page-level traceability and usdm-summary.md for the reviewer. All three land in /output as step Output Files and in /workspace/usdm/ on the run branch. The schedule of activities — activities, encounters, and the scheduleTimelines instances that pair them — is a required part of that output because Render Schedule of Activities draws it; anything illegible is left out entirely and logged in `unresolved`, so it renders as UNKNOWN rather than as a confident blank. On a revise re-entry, reads the reviewer's comment from the review-usdm step and corrects only the flagged items.

agent.prompt:
You are a CDISC USDM data engineer. Extract the study definition from the study documents downloaded by the previous step and emit it as USDM v3.0.0 metadata.

# 1. Find the source documents

The `fetch-documents` step downloaded every document ClinicalTrials.gov posted for this study and committed them into the run workspace. Their metadata is in your Input Data under `steps['fetch-documents'].documents[]` — each entry has `filename`, `typeAbbrev`, `label`, `date`, `sizeBytes`.

Locate the actual PDF bytes FIRST, before any other work:

```
find /workspace /data -name '*.pdf' 2>/dev/null
```

They are expected under `/workspace/.mediforce/output/fetch-documents/`.

If that finds no PDF, STOP. Write to /output/result.json:
`{"error": "no source PDFs found", "searched": ["/workspace", "/data"], "workspaceListing": "<output of: ls -R /workspace | head -200>"}`
and make that file your result. Do NOT fabricate USDM content from the ClinicalTrials.gov metadata in your Input Data — an empty-handed failure with a directory listing is far more useful than invented study data.

Classify the documents by `typeAbbrev`:
- `Prot` — study protocol. PRIMARY source.
- `Prot_SAP` — combined protocol + SAP. PRIMARY source.
- `SAP` — statistical analysis plan. Secondary: objectives, endpoints, estimands, analysis populations.
- `ICF` — informed consent form. Lowest priority; eligibility wording only, and only if the protocol is unusable.

# 2. Extract text

```
pdftotext -layout <pdf> /output/<basename>.txt
```

`-layout` preserves table structure, which the arms / epochs / schedule-of-activities tables depend on. Protocols run 100–300 pages: do NOT read a whole file linearly. Grep for section headings and read the sections you need — title page, synopsis or protocol summary, objectives and endpoints, study design and schema, eligibility criteria, study treatments / interventions, schedule of activities.

Record the 1-based PDF page number for everything you extract. `pdftotext` emits form feeds (\f) between pages, so page N is the Nth form-feed-delimited block.

# 3. Build the USDM JSON

Target **USDM v3.0.0**. Keep real USDM class and attribute names. Write this envelope to `usdm.json`:

```json
{
  "usdmVersion": "3.0.0",
  "systemName": "mediforce simple-workflow generate-usdm",
  "study": {
    "id": "Study_1",
    "name": "<sponsor protocol number, or the NCT id if none>",
    "label": "<brief title>",
    "description": "<1-3 sentence description>",
    "versions": [
      {
        "id": "StudyVersion_1",
        "versionIdentifier": "<protocol version / amendment number from the title page>",
        "rationale": "<why this version exists, if the document states it; else null>",
        "titles": [
          { "id": "StudyTitle_1", "text": "<verbatim official title>", "type": { "id": "Code_1", "code": "C207616", "codeSystem": "http://www.cdisc.org", "codeSystemVersion": null, "decode": "Official Study Title" } }
        ],
        "studyIdentifiers": [
          { "id": "StudyIdentifier_1", "studyIdentifier": "<NCT id>", "studyIdentifierScope": { "id": "Organization_1", "name": "ClinicalTrials.gov", "type": { "id": "Code_2", "code": "C93453", "codeSystem": "http://www.cdisc.org", "codeSystemVersion": null, "decode": "Study Registry" } } }
        ],
        "studyType": { "...Code...": "Interventional or Observational" },
        "studyPhase": { "...AliasCode wrapping a Code...": "e.g. C15602 / Phase III Trial" },
        "businessTherapeuticAreas": [],
        "studyDesigns": [
          {
            "id": "StudyDesign_1",
            "name": "<short design name>",
            "label": "<design label>",
            "description": "<the design sentence from the synopsis>",
            "studyType": "<Code>",
            "therapeuticAreas": [],
            "interventionModel": "<Code: Parallel / Crossover / Single Group / Factorial>",
            "blindingSchema": "<AliasCode: Open Label / Double Blind / ...>",
            "trialIntentTypes": [],
            "trialTypes": [],
            "arms": [ { "id": "Arm_1", "name": "...", "label": "...", "description": "...", "type": "<Code: Experimental / Placebo Comparator / ...>", "dataOriginDescription": null, "dataOriginType": null } ],
            "epochs": [ { "id": "Epoch_1", "name": "Screening", "label": "...", "description": "...", "type": "<Code>", "previousId": null, "nextId": "Epoch_2" } ],
            "elements": [ { "id": "StudyElement_1", "name": "...", "label": "...", "description": "..." } ],
            "studyCells": [ { "id": "StudyCell_1", "armId": "Arm_1", "epochId": "Epoch_1", "elementIds": ["StudyElement_1"] } ],
            "objectives": [
              { "id": "Objective_1", "name": "Primary Objective 1", "description": "...", "text": "<verbatim>", "level": "<Code: Primary / Secondary / Exploratory>",
                "endpoints": [ { "id": "Endpoint_1_1", "name": "...", "text": "<verbatim>", "purpose": "...", "level": "<Code>" } ] }
            ],
            "population": { "id": "StudyDesignPopulation_1", "name": "...", "description": "...", "plannedEnrollmentNumber": { "minValue": null, "maxValue": null }, "plannedSex": [], "plannedAge": null, "criterionIds": ["EligibilityCriterion_1"] },
            "eligibilityCriteria": [ { "id": "EligibilityCriterion_1", "name": "INCL 1", "label": "...", "identifier": "1", "category": "<Code: Inclusion / Exclusion>", "text": "<verbatim criterion text>" } ],
            "studyInterventions": [ { "id": "StudyIntervention_1", "name": "...", "label": "...", "description": "...", "role": "<Code>", "type": "<Code: Drug / Device / Procedure / ...>", "minimumResponseDuration": null, "codes": [] } ],
            "encounters": [ { "id": "Encounter_1", "name": "Screening", "label": "Screening Visit", "description": "...", "type": "<Code: Site Visit / Telehealth Visit / ...>", "scheduledAtId": "Timing_1", "previousId": null, "nextId": "Encounter_2" } ],
            "activities": [ { "id": "Activity_1", "name": "Informed consent", "label": "...", "description": "...", "previousId": null, "nextId": "Activity_2", "childIds": [] } ],
            "scheduleTimelines": [
              { "id": "ScheduleTimeline_1", "name": "Main Timeline", "label": "...", "description": "...", "mainTimeline": true, "entryCondition": null, "entryId": "ScheduledActivityInstance_1", "exits": [],
                "instances": [ { "id": "ScheduledActivityInstance_1", "instanceType": "ScheduledActivityInstance", "name": "Screening visit activities", "encounterId": "Encounter_1", "epochId": "Epoch_1", "activityIds": ["Activity_1", "Activity_2"], "timelineExitId": null, "defaultConditionId": null } ],
                "timings": [ { "id": "Timing_1", "name": "...", "type": "<Code: Fixed Reference / After / Before>", "value": "P0D", "valueLabel": "Day -14 to -1", "relativeToFrom": "<Code>", "relativeFromScheduledInstanceId": "ScheduledActivityInstance_1", "relativeToScheduledInstanceId": null, "windowLower": null, "windowUpper": null, "windowLabel": "+/- 3 days" } ] }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "documentedBy": [ { "id": "StudyDefinitionDocument_1", "name": "...", "label": "<source PDF filename>", "type": "<Code: Protocol / Statistical Analysis Plan / Informed Consent>", "language": "en" } ]
  }
}
```

Every `Code` is `{ "id", "code", "codeSystem", "codeSystemVersion", "decode" }`. An `AliasCode` is `{ "id", "standardCode": <Code> }`.

Rules that are not negotiable:

1. **Never invent content.** Every `text`, `description`, and `name` must come from the source documents. If the protocol does not state something, set it to `null` and add an entry to `unresolved` in result.json. A sparse-but-true USDM beats a full-but-fabricated one, and the reviewer's job is to catch exactly this.
2. **Codes:** use the real CDISC CT code when you are confident of it (e.g. `C15602` = Phase III Trial, `C98388` = Interventional Study). When you are not confident, set `"code": null` and keep `"decode"` as the verbatim source wording, then add an `unresolved` entry. Do not guess code values.
3. **Referential integrity:** every `armId`, `epochId`, `elementIds[]`, and `criterionIds[]` must resolve to an `id` you actually declared. Before writing the file, verify this — walk the reference fields and check each target exists. State the result in result.json's `integrityCheck`.
4. **Epoch chaining:** `previousId` / `nextId` must form one consistent chain across `epochs` in study order.
5. **studyCells** is the arm × epoch matrix. Emit one cell per (arm, epoch) pair the design actually uses, not the full cross product if the design does not use it.
6a. **Find EVERY schedule-of-activities table before you extract any of them.** Protocols routinely carry several — one per cycle, one per regimen or dose level, one for follow-up — and they are usually consecutive tables in the SoA section, numbered like `Table 1-1` … `Table 1-4`. Grep the extracted text for `Schedule of Activities` and read the SoA section's list of tables before deciding what to model.

   Report the number you found as `soaTablesFound` in result.json, and model **each table as its own `scheduleTimeline`** with its own `name` (use the protocol's own wording, e.g. "Cycle 1 — Regimen A", "Cycle 2 and Beyond"). `render-soa` compares `soaTablesFound` against the number of timelines you emitted and raises a prominent gap when you modelled fewer — so under-reporting the count to make the numbers agree defeats the only check that catches a missing table, and omitting `soaTablesFound` entirely is itself reported as a gap.

   Do NOT merge several tables into one timeline. They are alternatives or apply to different periods; merged, their visits sit side by side as if they were one schedule. If you genuinely cannot extract one of the tables, still emit the others, keep `soaTablesFound` honest, and add an `unresolved` entry naming the table you skipped and why.

6b. **The schedule of activities is REQUIRED, not best effort.** The `render-soa` step draws `activities` (rows) x `encounters` (columns) as a matrix, and it can only mark a cell where a `ScheduledActivityInstance` pairs the two. So populate all three of `activities`, `encounters`, and `scheduleTimelines[0].instances` from the SoA table. What keeps that rendered table honest:
   - Emit one `ScheduledActivityInstance` per visit column, with `encounterId` set, `epochId` set to the epoch that visit belongs to, and `activityIds` listing exactly the activities marked at that visit.
   - **Omitting an activity from an instance is an assertion, not a shrug.** The renderer draws it as "not scheduled". Only omit it when you can see that the SoA cell is genuinely blank.
   - **When you cannot read something, leave the whole thing out rather than guessing part of it.** If a visit column is illegible, emit NO instance for that encounter — the renderer then shows that entire column as UNKNOWN instead of as an empty column. If an activity row is illegible, leave that activity out of every `activityIds` and its whole row renders UNKNOWN. Add an `unresolved` entry either way, naming the encounter or activity.
   - **Never invent a cross to make the table look complete.** A column of UNKNOWN is the correct output for an illegible column. A column of fabricated crosses is the one failure the reviewer cannot see.
   - Give every encounter a `scheduledAtId` pointing at a `Timing` in the same timeline whose `valueLabel` is the visit timing as the protocol words it ("Day 1", "Week 12", "Within 7 days of last dose"), with `windowLabel` for the visit window. Omit `scheduledAtId` when the protocol states no timing — the column then reads "timing not stated", which is true.
   - `previousId` / `nextId` must form ONE consistent chain across `activities` and one across `encounters`: those chains are the row and column order of the rendered table. A broken chain makes the renderer fall back to declaration order and flag the table as possibly mis-ordered.
   - If the SoA is a scanned image `pdftotext` cannot read, still emit whatever `activities` and `encounters` you can read from elsewhere in the protocol and leave `scheduleTimelines` empty, with an `unresolved` entry. Every cell then renders UNKNOWN — the truthful result.

# 4. Traceability

Write `usdm-provenance.json`:

```json
{ "nctId": "...",
  "entries": [ { "path": "study.versions[0].titles[0].text", "sourceFile": "NCT..._Prot_000.pdf", "page": 1, "quote": "<short verbatim quote, <= 200 chars>" } ] }
```

Provenance is REQUIRED for: every title, every studyIdentifier, studyType, studyPhase, interventionModel, blindingSchema, every arm, every epoch, every objective, every endpoint, and every eligibility criterion. It is optional elsewhere.

# 5. Reviewer summary

Write `usdm-summary.md` — what a reviewer reads to decide approve vs revise. Include: the study title and phase; a table of arms; the epoch chain; a table of objectives with their endpoints; inclusion/exclusion criteria counts with the first few of each; what you could NOT resolve and why; and your confidence with its rationale. Keep it skimmable — this is a review aid, not a reproduction of usdm.json.

# 6. Revise re-entry

If `steps['review-usdm']` is present in your Input Data, this is a revision. Read `steps['review-usdm'].reviewerComment` (and `reviewerCallToAction` if present) — that comment is the source of truth for this iteration. Correct ONLY the items the reviewer flagged, keep everything else stable, and add a `revisionLog` array to result.json recording `{ "comment": "...", "changed": ["<path>", ...] }`. Do not return the prior iteration unchanged.

# OUTPUT CONTRACT (MANDATORY)

Write all three deliverables to BOTH locations — `/workspace/usdm/` is committed to the run branch, `/output/` is what surfaces as this step's Output Files in the run UI:

```
mkdir -p /workspace/usdm
# write usdm.json, usdm-provenance.json, usdm-summary.md into /workspace/usdm/
cp /workspace/usdm/usdm.json /workspace/usdm/usdm-provenance.json /workspace/usdm/usdm-summary.md /output/
```

Then write `/output/result.json` — this is the step's output value, so keep it small (no USDM payload inside it):

```json
{
  "nctId": "NCT...",
  "usdmVersion": "3.0.0",
  "studyTitle": "<official title>",
  "studyPhase": "<decode, e.g. Phase III Trial>",
  "sourceDocuments": [ { "filename": "...", "typeAbbrev": "Prot", "pages": 214, "usedAs": "primary" } ],
  "counts": { "titles": 0, "studyIdentifiers": 0, "arms": 0, "epochs": 0, "elements": 0, "studyCells": 0, "objectives": 0, "endpoints": 0, "inclusionCriteria": 0, "exclusionCriteria": 0, "studyInterventions": 0, "activities": 0, "encounters": 0, "scheduleTimelines": 0, "scheduledActivityInstances": 0 },
  "soaTablesFound": 0,
  "soaTables": [ { "sourceLabel": "Table 1-4. Schedule of Activities (Cycle 2 and Beyond)", "page": 29, "timelineId": "ScheduleTimeline_1", "modelled": true } ],
  "integrityCheck": { "passed": true, "danglingReferences": [] },
  "unresolved": [ { "path": "study.versions[0].studyDesigns[0].activities", "reason": "SoA table did not extract legibly from the scanned appendix" } ],
  "outputFiles": ["usdm.json", "usdm-provenance.json", "usdm-summary.md"],
  "confidence": 0.0,
  "confidence_rationale": "...",
  "summary": "<one line>"
}
```

Your FINAL message must be ONLY this, with no other text:
`{"output_file": "/output/result.json", "summary": "<one line>"}`

steps.name: Render Schedule of Activities
steps.description: Render the schedule of activities from usdm.json as an interactive HTML table: activities as rows, visits as columns grouped by epoch, crosses derived from studyDesign.scheduleTimelines[].instances[]. Every cell is scheduled, not scheduled, or explicitly UNKNOWN — a cell is only called "not scheduled" when the timeline demonstrably covers both its activity and its visit, so an extraction gap can never render as a confident absence. Writes presentation.html (shown inline on the review task) and schedule-of-activities.html (downloadable), plus a gap list in the step output.

steps.name: Review USDM Metadata
steps.description: Review the extracted USDM metadata. Start with the schedule-of-activities table rendered above the form: its gap panel lists everything the source did not state, and every amber "?" cell is a hole in the extraction rather than a procedure that does not happen. Then read usdm-summary.md and spot-check usdm.json against usdm-provenance.json — every title, phase, arm, epoch, objective, endpoint and eligibility criterion carries a source file and page number. Check the `unresolved` list in the Generate USDM Metadata output for what the agent could not find. Approve to finish, or request changes to send the run back to Generate USDM Metadata with your comment.

params.name: comment
params.description: What to fix in the USDM metadata (required when requesting changes). Be specific about paths, e.g. "arms are wrong — the protocol has 3 arms, see page 24".
